newsitem.title: USA: Iowa corn declines, soybeans see improvement.
newsitem.headline: Iowa corn declines, soybeans see improvement.

text.p: A hot humid week spurred growth in the Iowa corn and soybean crops, but dry conditions hurt the crops in some areas during the week ended Sunday, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

"Many areas in the west central and southern districts were very dry, and many of those locations received rain on Sunday," the report said. "The scattered rains, however, may leave many fields thirsty for more precipitation."
Corn had tasseled on 28 percent percent of the state's acreage, versus two percent last week, 11 percent last year and the five-year average of 35 percent.
Corn conditions declined from a week ago and were three percent poor, 21 percent fair, 56 percent good and 20 percent excellent as of Friday.
Soybeans were blooming in Iowa on 60 percent of the acreage as of Sunday. That compares to 33 percent last week, 43 percent last year and the five-year average of 53 percent.
The soybean condition improved last week to four percent poor, 24 percent fair, 56 percent good and 16 percent excellent as of Friday.
Topsoil moisture as of Friday was 11 percent very short, 37 percent short, 49 percent adequate and three percent surplus.
